{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py",
      "line": 482,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "User validation is skipped when the Integration row does not exist",
      "body": "GitHubInstallation.dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() when Integration.DoesNotExist, before any installer validation. The new OAuth-user check only runs when an active Integration row already exists. If the webhook that creates the Integration is delayed or fails, if the row has been deleted, or if an installation_id is supplied directly, the pipeline can create/claim a GitHub installation without verifying that the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user installed the app. This is a fail-open bypass of the stated mismatch protection. The flow should fail closed or otherwise verify installer identity before advancing when no Integration/sender data is available."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py",
      "line": 503,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Direct metadata access can crash when sender is missing",
      "body": "The sender comparison accesses integration.metadata['sender']['login'] unconditionally. If metadata is missing, sender is missing, or sender lacks login (for example, integrations created without a webhook sender, older integrations, or failed webhooks), this raises KeyError/TypeError and returns a 500 instead of the intended error page. Use safe access and return the installation-failed error when the required sender identity is absent."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py",
      "line": 503,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Matching on mutable GitHub login instead of immutable user ID",
      "body": "The implementation binds and compares GitHub logins. GitHub logins are mutable and can be renamed; old logins may later be registered by another user. This can block a legitimate installer after a rename and, in the worse case, allow a different user who acquired the old login to satisfy the check. Use the stable GitHub user ID from both the webhook sender and OAuth user info, and fail if IDs are unavailable."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py",
      "line": 478,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Integration lookups omit provider filter",
      "body": "Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) is used without filtering provider='github' (also at line 494). If external_id is unique only per provider, an ID collision with another integration provider can return the wrong Integration or raise MultipleObjectsReturned. That can cause false 'installed on another org' errors, wrong sender metadata being checked, or crashes. Add provider=GitHubIntegrationProvider.key to these queries."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py",
      "line": 448,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "installation_id can be changed after the OAuth step",
      "body": "GitHubInstallation.dispatch takes installation_id from request.GET in preference to the value bound during the OAuth step and overwrites pipeline state with it. After OAuth has completed, a URL can therefore retarget the pipeline to a different installation_id without re-validating that choice against the OAuth flow. Combined with the missing validation for absent Integration rows, this allows an installation_id to be switched mid-pipeline. If the query parameter must be accepted for direct installs, compare it with the bound state or fail when they differ, and validate the installer for the final installation_id."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py",
      "line": 423,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "OAuth exchange failures can raise 500s",
      "body": "safe_urlopen and get_user_info are not wrapped in the same exception handling as the token-response parsing. A network failure, timeout, non-200 response, or GitHub API error during token exchange/user-info fetch will bubble up as a 500 instead of rendering the installation-failed page. Catch the expected HTTP/API errors and return error(...)."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py",
      "line": 408,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "OAuth authorize URL parameters are not URL-encoded",
      "body": "The GitHub authorize URL is constructed with an f-string instead of URL encoding the query parameters. redirect_uri (and any future parameters) is inserted raw, which can produce an invalid authorize URL if it contains reserved characters and is generally error-prone. Build the query string with urllib.parse.urlencode."
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py",
      "line": 399,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Tests do not cover missing sender metadata or absent Integration rows",
      "body": "test_github_user_mismatch only covers the case where a webhook-created Integration has metadata.sender.login. There are no tests for the security-relevant paths where metadata.sender is absent or where no Integration row exists before installation. Those paths currently crash or bypass the user-match check, so add regression tests for them."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: User validation is skipped when the Integration row does not exist
findings.body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() when Integration.DoesNotExist, before any installer validation. The new OAuth-user check only runs when an active Integration row already exists. If the webhook that creates the Integration is delayed or fails, if the row has been deleted, or if an installation_id is supplied directly, the pipeline can create/claim a GitHub installation without verifying that the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user installed the app. This is a fail-open bypass of the stated mismatch protection. The flow should fail closed or otherwise verify installer identity before advancing when no Integration/sender data is available.

findings.title: Direct metadata access can crash when sender is missing
findings.body: The sender comparison accesses integration.metadata['sender']['login'] unconditionally. If metadata is missing, sender is missing, or sender lacks login (for example, integrations created without a webhook sender, older integrations, or failed webhooks), this raises KeyError/TypeError and returns a 500 instead of the intended error page. Use safe access and return the installation-failed error when the required sender identity is absent.

findings.title: Matching on mutable GitHub login instead of immutable user ID
findings.body: The implementation binds and compares GitHub logins. GitHub logins are mutable and can be renamed; old logins may later be registered by another user. This can block a legitimate installer after a rename and, in the worse case, allow a different user who acquired the old login to satisfy the check. Use the stable GitHub user ID from both the webhook sender and OAuth user info, and fail if IDs are unavailable.

findings.title: Integration lookups omit provider filter
findings.body: Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) is used without filtering provider='github' (also at line 494). If external_id is unique only per provider, an ID collision with another integration provider can return the wrong Integration or raise MultipleObjectsReturned. That can cause false 'installed on another org' errors, wrong sender metadata being checked, or crashes. Add provider=GitHubIntegrationProvider.key to these queries.

findings.title: installation_id can be changed after the OAuth step
findings.body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch takes installation_id from request.GET in preference to the value bound during the OAuth step and overwrites pipeline state with it. After OAuth has completed, a URL can therefore retarget the pipeline to a different installation_id without re-validating that choice against the OAuth flow. Combined with the missing validation for absent Integration rows, this allows an installation_id to be switched mid-pipeline. If the query parameter must be accepted for direct installs, compare it with the bound state or fail when they differ, and validate the installer for the final installation_id.

findings.title: OAuth exchange failures can raise 500s
findings.body: safe_urlopen and get_user_info are not wrapped in the same exception handling as the token-response parsing. A network failure, timeout, non-200 response, or GitHub API error during token exchange/user-info fetch will bubble up as a 500 instead of rendering the installation-failed page. Catch the expected HTTP/API errors and return error(...).

findings.title: OAuth authorize URL parameters are not URL-encoded
findings.body: The GitHub authorize URL is constructed with an f-string instead of URL encoding the query parameters. redirect_uri (and any future parameters) is inserted raw, which can produce an invalid authorize URL if it contains reserved characters and is generally error-prone. Build the query string with urllib.parse.urlencode.

findings.title: Tests do not cover missing sender metadata or absent Integration rows
findings.body: test_github_user_mismatch only covers the case where a webhook-created Integration has metadata.sender.login. There are no tests for the security-relevant paths where metadata.sender is absent or where no Integration row exists before installation. Those paths currently crash or bypass the user-match check, so add regression tests for them.
